Power generation NDT training in Charlotte: the short answer

Power generation NDT training in Charlotte prepares technicians for boiler tube, header, piping, turbine and heat-exchanger inspection at Carolinas fossil, combined-cycle and combustion-turbine stations, and in the turbine and generator manufacturing plants around the city. Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, live online or onsite at your facility, led by an ASNT Level III. Quotes are on request.

This page covers non-nuclear power generation: coal, gas and combined-cycle plants, outage contractors, and the manufacturing and repair shops that supply them. Nuclear work runs under a different set of rules and is covered on our nuclear NDT training in Charlotte page. Keeping the two apart matters, because a technician who is perfectly qualified for a boiler outage may need several more steps before working inside a nuclear plant.

Request a Charlotte power generation NDT training quote, or read on.

Power generation NDT work in Charlotte

Charlotte is the headquarters city of Duke Energy, whose Carolinas generating fleet includes coal, natural gas, combined-cycle, combustion-turbine, hydro and nuclear stations within reach of the metro. Examples of non-nuclear stations in the region include the Marshall Steam Station on Lake Norman, the Rogers Energy Complex at Cliffside, the Buck Combined Cycle Station near Salisbury and the Lincoln Combustion Turbine Station. We name these only as context for where power-generation NDT happens; Atlantis has no relationship with Duke Energy and does not claim one.

The city is also a manufacturing base for the power industry. Siemens Energy's Charlotte Energy Hub builds gas turbines for 60 Hz markets alongside steam turbine and generator work, and a supply chain of fabricators, machine shops and repair facilities has grown around it and around the utility fleet. Also in Charlotte is the EPRI laboratory campus on W.T. Harris Boulevard, home of the long-established EPRI NDE Center, which researches inspection, welding and materials technology for the power industry. EPRI is context here: it is a research organisation, not a training provider for this page's audience, and Atlantis is not affiliated with it.

For an NDT technician that adds up to three kinds of work:

  • Outage inspection. Planned spring and fall outages at fossil and combined-cycle units, when boilers, heat-recovery steam generators (HRSGs), headers, piping, turbines and condensers are opened and every deferred inspection happens at once.
  • Manufacturing and repair. Year-round inspection of turbine components, generator parts, welded casings, pressure parts and repaired components to construction codes.
  • Condition monitoring. Thickness surveys, flow-accelerated corrosion programmes and creep-damage assessment between outages.

Specialist tube techniques used in power plants, such as IRIS, remote-field and EMAT, are not part of our course list; we mention them as context. Our SNT-TC-1A courses give the method foundation those techniques build on. Start with the UT Level II course for most boiler and piping work, or the ET Level II course for tubing.

A method spotlight for Charlotte: UT on boiler tubes and headers

Boiler tube failures are the most common cause of forced outages at fossil units, and most are found or prevented with ultrasonic thickness readings and weld inspection. The difficulty is not the instrument; it is technique under outage conditions: scale and oxide on the tube surface, curved and thin walls, limited access, scaffolding, and a schedule that gives a crew a fixed window. Technicians need to understand couplant and surface prep, dual-element probes, thickness on oxide-coated tubes, and how to record readings so an engineer can trend them across outages. On headers and piping, the shift is to angle-beam and PAUT inspection of welds, where knowing dissimilar-metal weld behaviour and creep damage patterns matters. Our onsite training uses your own calibration standards and, where available, removed tube samples.

Combined-cycle and gas turbine work around Charlotte

As the Carolinas generating mix has shifted toward natural gas, more of the region's power-generation NDT happens on combined-cycle plants and gas turbines rather than on coal boilers. That changes the inspection scope. Heat-recovery steam generators cycle on and off far more often than a base-load coal boiler, so thermal fatigue at tube-to-header welds, attemperator and drain-line damage, and flow-accelerated corrosion in low-pressure sections become the priorities. Access inside an HRSG is tight, and much of the work is UT thickness, PAUT on small-bore welds and VT with borescopes. Gas turbines bring PT and ET on blades, vanes and combustion hardware during hot-gas-path inspections, mostly under OEM procedures, and MT on casings and rotor features during major overhauls. Turbine and generator manufacturing in Charlotte adds production inspection of castings, forgings and welded fabrications to construction codes. A technician who understands both the outage side and the manufacturing side is valuable here, and SNT-TC-1A certification in UT, MT and PT covers the core of both.

The SNT-TC-1A path in Charlotte, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer owns the written practice that sets training, experience and exam rules. If you need one, see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Method theory, equipment, technique, ASME and owner procedures. Hours depend on method and level; see the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged under a certified technician; outage seasons build this quickly.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. Administered by a Level III, using the procedures your crews actually work to.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision and colour contrast, renewed annually.
  6. Employer certification and recertification. Following the written practice.

Employers can read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing, plant access and boiler rules in the Charlotte region

North Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive material used in industrial radiography is licensed by the state's Radiation Protection Section in the Department of Health and Human Services, and radiographers must meet the certification and training requirements that come with those licences. Charlotte crews often cross into South Carolina, which has its own state radiation programme. Check the current requirements in each state before RT work. Atlantis teaches radiographic technique and interpretation; we do not issue radiation safety credentials.

Fossil and gas stations have their own site access, safety orientation and contractor qualification requirements, set by the owner. Boiler and pressure-vessel repairs follow the National Board Inspection Code and state boiler law; in North Carolina the Department of Labor runs the boiler safety programme. None of these is NDT certification, but each affects how quickly a new technician can start on site.

How Atlantis delivers power generation NDT training to Charlotte

We have no training centre in Charlotte. We deliver in three ways:

  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III-led course at your Charlotte shop or yard, on your equipment and reference standards, timed before the outage season.
  • Live online. Real-time classroom sessions for individuals and small groups. See online NDT training.
  • Blended. Theory online, then an onsite block for practicals and examinations.

Outage contractors usually want new hires qualified before the spring and fall peaks, so we plan backwards from your outage calendar. Ask about onsite training before your next outage. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day; see corporate NDT training.

Level III services and written practices for Charlotte power-sector companies

Outage contractors and repair shops in the Charlotte region often need outside Level III help: a written practice that satisfies an owner's vendor audit, examinations for a batch of new hires, procedure and technique-sheet review, or preparation for an ASME or National Board audit. Atlantis provides Level III services under SNT-TC-1A. For consulting in the region see NDT consulting in Charlotte, or book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments, including an NDT lab, a welding workshop and a storage tank, which cover much of the scanning technique used on power-plant welds and thickness work. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens. Local users can start at Practical NDT for Charlotte.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work.

Frequently asked questions about power generation NDT training in Charlotte

Where can I get power plant NDT training in Charlotte?

CPCC runs a college NDE programme, outage contractors train their own crews, and Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A training live online or onsite at your Charlotte facility.

Which NDT method is most in demand for power plant outages?

UT, for boiler tube thickness and weld inspection, followed by ET for condenser and heat-exchanger tubing and MT and PT during turbine overhauls.

Is fossil power plant NDT different from nuclear NDT?

Yes. Fossil and gas plants work to ASME Section I, B31.1 and owner programmes, usually with SNT-TC-1A certified personnel. Nuclear plants add ASME Section XI, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programmes, often CP-189, and PDI for some UT. See our nuclear NDT training in Charlotte page.

How long does UT Level II training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A it depends on your written practice: classroom hours plus on-the-job experience. See the training requirements matrix.

Can I take NDT training online in North Carolina?

Yes, the classroom portion can be taken live online. Practical exams are done on real specimens, usually at your employer's facility.

Do I need a license for radiography in North Carolina?

Radioactive sources are licensed by the state's Radiation Protection Section, and radiographers must meet certification and training requirements. NDT training alone does not license you. Work in South Carolina falls under that state's programme.

What does power generation NDT training cost in Charlotte?

We quote on request. Cost depends on methods, levels, group size, online versus onsite delivery, and whether exams and written-practice work are included. Onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can you qualify our crew before the spring outage?

Often, if we start early enough to cover classroom training and your written practice's experience requirements. Tell us your outage dates.

Do you offer IRIS, EMAT or PDI training?

No. Atlantis trains UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under SNT-TC-1A, plus Level III preparation. Specialist techniques and PDI are context only.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training in Charlotte?

Generally only at approved schools and programmes. Atlantis does not claim that approval; employer sponsorship is the usual route for our courses. NCWorks and the VA can confirm approved local options.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Charlotte power-sector employers?

SNT-TC-1A certification is the norm for fossil and combined-cycle contractors and power-equipment manufacturers. Owners may add their own vendor requirements on top.

What do power plant NDT technicians earn?

We do not publish city salary figures. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges and sources.
